headline_cluster.headline: למה יד אחת שלנו טובה יותר מהשנייה? מחקר חדש מציע תשובה מפתיעה

claims.claim_he_or_en: רק כ-10 אחוזים מאוכלוסיית העולם הם אטרי יד ימין, כלומר שמאליים, ואילו היתר ימניים
claims.verified_figure: 10.6% pooled best estimate (10.4% excl. elite athletes); range 9.3%-18.1% by definition; ~9.3% mixed-handed where measured (Papadatou-Pastou et al., Psychol Bull 2020, ~2.4M people)
claims.note: 'About 10%' matches the largest meta-analysis. Minor simplification: 'the rest are right-handed' ignores the mixed-handed category, but the headline figure is correct. Not sourced in the PNAS paper (which says only 'most people are right-handed').

claims.claim_he_or_en: עדויות ארכיאולוגיות מצביעות על כך שהעדפת יד ימין הייתה נפוצה יותר משמאליות כבר כמיליון שנה
claims.verified_figure: Earliest fossil indication: OH-65 (Olduvai, ~1.8 Mya) labial tooth striations, a single specimen (Frayer et al., J Hum Evol 2016). Population-level evidence (Sima de los Huesos, Neanderthal dental striations) dates to ~0.4-0.5 Mya.
claims.note: No source given and the figure is not in the PNAS paper. The literature supports right-hand preference somewhere between ~0.5 Mya (robust, population-level) and ~1.8 Mya (one specimen); 'about a million years' is a loose midpoint rather than a cited figure, and stating 'more common than left-handedness' that far back overstates what one specimen shows.

claims.claim_he_or_en: מחקר חדש, שפורסם בכתב העת PNAS
claims.note: Study exists in PNAS as described. ynet did not name authors or institutions (UCLA / Johns Hopkins); the Davidson Institute credit is for the write-up, not the research.

claims.claim_he_or_en: 23 נבדקים ימניים התבקשו לגעת עם כף היד בחמש נקודות במרחב בשלושה תנאים; בתנאי הבסיס יתרון קטן בלבד ליד הדומיננטית
claims.verified_figure: Regular reaches: 23 subjects, 5 targets, palm touch; all right-handed healthy young adults. Discussion: 'we only observed a small difference in trajectory variance in favor of the dominant arm.'
claims.note: Minor nuance: the 23/10/11 counts are per condition (not all 23 did all three conditions); ynet's text then gives the separate n for conditions 2-3, which is consistent with the paper.

claims.claim_he_or_en: החוקרים חיברו לפרק היד של עשרה מהנבדקים משקולת של כ-1.8 ק"ג — לא נמצאה עדיפות ליד ימין
claims.verified_figure: 4 lb (=1.81 kg) wrist weight, 10 subjects; variance increased equally in both arms; weight reaches did not differ from regular reaches on any principal axis
claims.note: Paper explicitly frames the weight condition as the test of DDH, which predicted a dominant advantage that did not appear.

claims.claim_he_or_en: החוקרים חיברו לאמה של 11 מהנבדקים מקל ארוך וקל — נמצא יתרון מובהק ליד ימין הדומיננטית
claims.verified_figure: Very light (83 g) bamboo stick, extending 20 in. beyond mid-palm, 11 subjects; 'strong dominant advantage, driven by poor nondominant control of the stick-tip trajectory'

claims.claim_he_or_en: 11 נבדקים נדרשו לכתוב עם המרפק — לא נמצא יתרון למרפק של היד הדומיננטית
claims.verified_figure: 11 healthy subjects wrote 'A' and '8' with hands and elbows; 'no significant differences or trends between the dominant and nondominant elbow characters'
claims.note: Paper notes the nondominant side was slightly slower for both hand- and elbow-writing; shape quality showed no dominance effect.

claims.claim_he_or_en: 12 משתתפים חולקו לשתי קבוצות; אחרי כשעתיים של אימון שכלל כתיבה של כ-2,400 תווים — איכות הכתיבה של שתי הקבוצות השתפרה באותה מידה
claims.verified_figure: 12 subjects, 6 dominant-elbow / 6 nondominant-elbow; 2,400 practice characters; symmetric improvement, both surpassing nondominant-hand performance. Training duration not stated in main text (Science News: 'a few hours').
claims.note: Group sizes, character count and equal-improvement result verified. The '~2 hours' duration could not be confirmed (likely in SI appendix, not retrieved); it is consistent with press descriptions of 'a few hours'. ynet omits the paper's notable finding that trained elbows surpassed the nondominant hand.

claims.claim_he_or_en: המסקנה: היתרון נובע מאימון ותרגול לאורך שנים ולא מהתמחות מולדת של המוח (DDH); המחקר כלל מספר קטן של נבדקים, כולם צעירים וימניים
claims.verified_figure: Abstract: 'no general dominant limb motor control advantage, only task-specific experience or practice riding on top of an initial preference'; dominance reframed as 'learned control of tool kinematics rather than baseline asymmetry in control of limb dynamics.' All subjects right-handed, healthy, young adults.
claims.note: Matches the paper's conclusion. Nuance worth noting: the authors explicitly accept that hand PREFERENCE is innate/biological (present in utero); only the SKILL advantage is attributed to practice. Caveats in ynet (small n, young, right-handed) are factually correct; the paper itself has no formal limitations section but proposes follow-up with left-handers, stroke survivors and amputees.

primary_source.title: Arm dominance is an emergent effect of practice executing complex trajectory shapes required by tools and objects
primary_source.authors: Arac A, Lee NYHJ, Krakauer JW (UCLA; Johns Hopkins)
primary_source.access: Open access full text via Europe PMC (CC BY-NC-ND); SI appendix not retrieved

summary_verdict: All study-specific claims (sample sizes, conditions, results, conclusion) verified against open-access full text; general background figures accurate (10%) and imprecise (1 million years).
